name: Chin reduction / shaving

lead: Chin reduction is surgery to make a long, protruding or wide chin smaller. The aim is a more proportionate lower face, and the reduction is visible once healed.

The two classical approaches are an osteotomy that cuts the chin bone and moves it back or up (reduction or setback genioplasty), and burring the surface of the bone down. Another described approach removes bone and soft tissue from under the chin. It also appears alongside mandibular setback for a long chin and in feminization surgery. The published literature is technique descriptions and case series.

paras: Patients plan with a surgeon, who chooses between repositioning the bone and shaving it based on the shape of the chin. It is done under anaesthetic, and swelling settles over weeks to months before the final contour shows.

Surgical papers state that both main approaches have potential negative aesthetic sequelae, including mental nerve injury, bony contour irregularities, increased submental soft-tissue fullness and chin pad ptosis. It is performed under anaesthetic by licensed surgeons.

angle.text: Chin reduction shrinks a chin that looks too large or prominent by burring the bone or cutting and moving it back, for a smaller, better-proportioned lower face. The change is visible once healed. Techniques are described in surgical papers and case series.

lead: Chin reduction refers to surgical procedures that reduce the size of the chin in projection, height or width. A 1999 paper states that, at that time, surgical reduction of an isolated large chin was not a simple procedure, and that two operations existed: osteotomy with setback, or reduction of the prominence by burring. [1]

Reduction genioplasty is also used together with mandibular setback for prognathism and a long chin [2][3], and a box-shaped chin impaction osteotomy has been reported as part of mandibular feminization surgery. [4]
No trials comparing chin-reduction techniques were found; the literature consists of technique papers and case series. [1][5]
infobox: Setback or impaction osteotomy, burring, submental ostectomy
Nerve injury, contour irregularity, chin pad ptosis

paras: The 1999 paper describes osteotomy with setback and burring as the two classical operations, lists their potential sequelae, and presents a new approach of submental ostectomy with soft-tissue excision. [1] Another paper in the same series discusses key parameters for successful reduction of a large chin. [5]

A 1975 paper on chin reduction in profileplasty and a 1985 paper on physiological genioplasty are earlier descriptions. [6][7] A report of mandibular setback with reduction genioplasty for prognathism and long chin, and a 2020 paper on reduction genioplasty, describe the technique in the setting of skeletal discrepancies. [2][3]

Authors of a 2019 paper state that strong mandibular angles and a heavy chin are perceived as masculine and describe an osteotomy including a box-shaped impaction of the chin symphysis to reduce chin width and height. [4]

Potential negative aesthetic sequelae listed for both classical approaches include mental nerve injuries, bony contour irregularities, increased submental soft-tissue fullness and chin pad ptosis. [1]

Separately from bone reduction, submental fullness from fat has been the subject of registered trials of deoxycholic acid injection and device treatments, which address soft tissue rather than the chin bone. [8][9]

Published work includes technique descriptions and case reports of reduction genioplasty, setback with reduction genioplasty and feminization osteotomy. [1][2][3][4] Registered trials of submental fat reduction (for example NCT06256445, phase 3, n=252) address soft tissue rather than bone. [9]
